feedback_request.compare_against: Iteration 7 (mass 0.6, y = 0.08) for all three tracks, and iteration 6 (mass 0.6, y = 0.07) for the lead effect.

intent: Keep the iteration 7 geometry (y = 0.08 forward lead, 16 mm sensors, x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.16 by 0.14 m) and change only mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Integrator: keep kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, last_direction recovery, and the 25-times-x weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) with no gain change. Expected result: oval progress at or above 0.2725, s-bend progress at or above 0.1573 and closer to 0.1625, slalom progress at or above 0.1094, and slalom line losses at or below 1.0 per run. Decision rule for the next iteration: if s-bend progress falls below 0.1573 or slalom line losses exceed 1.0, restore mass 0.6 with y = 0.08 (the iteration 7 design). If s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.15, restore mass 0.6 and test wheel_track 0.11 at y = 0.08 as the single next change.
learning: Evidence so far: the forward lead is the main lever. y = 0.04 and 0.06 gave s-bend progress of 0.04. y = 0.07 gave 0.1625 to 0.165 and y = 0.08 gave 0.1573 on the s-bend but raised oval progress from 0.12 to 0.2725. Mass 0.8 to 0.6 lowered s-bend oscillation slightly and lifted oval progress marginally. Hypothesis A: a lighter robot (0.5 kg) holds the s-bend and slalom at the y = 0.08 lead while adding oval progress. Hypothesis B: the lighter robot over-responds, pushing oval and s-bend oscillation higher and losing the slalom line more often. If A holds, the next test is a narrower track at y = 0.08. If B holds, return to mass 0.6.
rationale:
Iteration 7 (y = 0.08, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, 16 mm sensors, 0.16 m spread) scored 75.92, the best result so far, up from 54.61 at y = 0.07. The gain came mainly from the oval, where progress rose from 0.12 to 0.2725 and oval score from 51 to 115. Oval max_error stayed at the 0.06 floor, so the oval was still at the edge but covered much more track. The s-bend fell slightly, from 0.1625 to 0.1573, and its oscillation was 0.135, under the 0.15 limit. Slalom progress was 0.1094 (above the 0.1075 threshold) with 1.0 line loss per run, which is within the limit I set.

My earlier pre-committed rule said to restore y = 0.07 if s-bend progress fell below 0.1625. I am not applying that rule. It was set before the oval gain was visible, and the overall score rose by 21 points. The s-bend loss is 0.005 of progress, while the oval gain is about 0.15 of progress on one track. Restoring y = 0.07 would give up the best-scoring design.

The design races once per seed, so repeating iteration 7 exactly would return the same result and teach us nothing. I therefore keep the y = 0.08 lead and sensor footprint and change one thing: mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Lower mass has already moved in the right direction. Going from 0.8 to 0.6 kg lowered s-bend oscillation (0.144 to 0.140) and lifted oval progress slightly (0.1175 to 0.12). The expected result is a further small reduction in yaw inertia, which should help the s-bend and slalom hold their progress at the stronger lead. The main risk is that a lighter robot over-responds on the oval, where steering oscillation already rose to 0.18 at y = 0.08. Oval oscillation is not one of the stated limits, but I will watch it.

The controller is unchanged, so this race isolates the mass step against iteration 7.
